chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Sayyabah and Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who said, 'The first slave I acquire is free,' and then he inherited three [other slaves]. He (the Imam) said, 'A lot is cast among them, and whoever the lot falls upon is freed.' He said, 'And casting lots is a Sunnah.'
ai.seo_question: How is the status of inherited slaves determined when a man has previously declared the first slave he acquires to be free?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *qur'ah* (casting lots) to resolve the ambiguity when a master's declaration of freeing the 'first acquired' slave conflicts with newly inherited slaves. The Imam establishes that casting lots is not merely a procedural formality but a *Sunnah* in itself, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of using chance to ensure impartiality in legal disputes. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on resolving conflicting obligations through divinely sanctioned methods of fairness.
